For instance, the diesel generators used for large-scale data centers are commonly 3.5 to 4.0 MW per unit, so building a 30.0- to 60.0-MW data center would require eight to 15 generators before accounting for redundancy. Scaling this approach to a one-GW data center would require up to 290 generators, and all of them would need to be maintained and prepared for a power loss situation, demonstrating the inefficiencies of the existing data center design methodology.
